## The late refusal

WI-10007452 reached the AWS image policy after an expensive publication build and was refused for unexplained bundled secret findings. The complete p012r69 census was reproduced with pinned gitleaks: server33, sidecar35, doc-vector manifest96, SPA3. The earlier hash-verified bundle reproduced its31 server findings. The difference was minified code, tokenizer data, and public page digests; each justification is recorded in `image-scan-secret-allowances.ts`. An additional finding still denies, and maxSecretFindings remains0.

## Check the same policy before cloud spend

The privacy auditor and the provider gitleaks policy answer different questions. `image-secret-scan.sh` now runs both on its existing digest-bound filesystem export, before signing. The provider-policy step reuses `applySecretAllowances` through `bootc-image-release-request-cli --emit bundled-secret-policy`; malformed reports and relative file paths refuse. Its output is explicitly preflightOnly, never image acceptance. Raw matches are deleted on success and failure. `bake-cloud-images.sh` resolves the evaluator/runner outside the frozen build-context copy and refuses missing tools before building. The full provider scan still runs at publication.

## Recover the existing private candidate

Use the existing `aws-ami-release-cli --resume-candidate-ami <exact-id>` only for a still-private encrypted candidate. The production adapter verifies local disk bytes, persisted publisher ownership, exact image name/Description/architecture/provenance/guest versions, one encrypted root snapshot, snapshot owner/size/CMK/provenance, and measured empty image/snapshot permissions. It refuses mismatches and already-shared candidates. Recovery performs no upload or copy; it returns to the normal fresh scan, sharing/encryption inspection, clean-account boot/teardown, manifest and pin gates. Preserve the failed phase evidence before retrying; do not replay the full upload or substitute an earlier release receipt.

Tests live in the existing allowance, AWS production, release CLI, bootc request, image-scan binding and bake snapshot suites. See WI-10007452 and aws-byoc-gcp-parity-2026-10-01 P-012. These procedures do not authorize a controller pin/restart; D-049 still requires trusted A/B publication followed by exclusive resource arbitration.

## Reserve the inherited execution budget

WI-10007501 measured a combined clean-room/publication task expiring at its three-hour hard deadline during scan. The clean room had already passed; encrypted copy readiness left four minutes for the remaining gates. `aws-ami-production.ts` now reads the existing launcher’s `PAPERCUSP_TASK_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` as an absolute bound and refuses insufficient remaining time before staging/publication/scan/canary. Absence means no measured parent bound, not a proven safe duration. Budgets reuse actual upload retries, regional image waits and the canonical rendered canary fixture/chunk count. Separate long phases into separately budgeted tasks; a child cannot extend its containing task’s deadline.

The scanner formerly inherited a45-minute parent timeout although its download permits60minutes. Its shared budgets now reserve download, three serial scans, bounded host work, teardown and margin. Individual commands shrink against an absolute work deadline, and teardown gets a separate bounded phase. These are declared phase limits, not elapsed-time predictions.

## Include SSM delivery time and preserve command identity

B recovery later failed when the service check remained Pending at200seconds. The actual SendCommand allowed600seconds of delivery plus180seconds of document execution. AWS subsequently reported Undeliverable with no execution start; this is not proof the service was inactive. [AWS total timeout includes delivery plus document execution.](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/monitor-commands.html)

The canary now shares `CANARY_BUDGETS.ssmDeliveryMs` between SendCommand, each total wait and the fixture-derived parent budget. Timeout evidence includes commandId, phase, delivery/execution budgets and last invocation details/start timestamp. Delayed-delivery and exhausted-delivery tests run in `aws-ami-canary.test.ts`; the actual parent budget is tested in `aws-ami-production.test.ts`. Preserve exact failed command metadata before instance teardown. A terminated guest’s original agent/network condition may remain unmeasured; never replace that gap with a service-failure guess.

## Contained formerly shared candidates use a distinct reviewed route

D-050 forbids removing sharing merely to feed a formerly shared candidate into the still-private option. After reviewed WI-10007515 implementation, the explicit `--contained-candidate-receipt-file <path>` route accepts operator custody evidence for a failed shared publication. First verify exact publisher/region/image/root snapshot, positive-control clean identity/subnet, terminated prior canary and zero scoped residue. Contain only the failed candidate’s permissions; preserve other releases and shared CMK grants. Persist `papercusp:contained-canary` on both image and snapshot, then read back matching markers and empty permissions. The original private option rejects a marker on either resource, even after sharing removal.

The explicit receipt binds image/snapshot/release/build/publisher/region/clean account/prior canary, requires observed termination, zero residue, an evidence reference and age≤1hour. The adapter independently remeasures immutable provenance/encryption/size and current permissions. The operator-authored receipt records custody; it is not a replacement for those AWS checks or for fresh scan, sharing/encryption inspection, clean-account launch/teardown, manifest and pin gates. A successful local test or containment action is not publication acceptance. See canonical suites and EI-25423084967590719 for the delivery-budget incident.
